subj: I tried estimating an ore body from a few drill holes
value: Build: Gaussian-process ore body estimator, grid vs uncertainty-guided drilling on 12 synthetic deposits
body:
Mineflow predicting deposit shapes made me curious how much a few drill holes can actually tell you, so I built a small version: a hidden synthetic ore body, vertical holes, and a Gaussian process (the math behind kriging) that estimates the shape.

The surprise was that choosing each next hole by where the model was least sure lost to a plain grid until about 36 holes. When the first scouting holes all miss a narrow body, the model thinks the claim is barren and sends holes to the edges. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/drillhole-ore-model

I'm sure you've thought about this far more than I have, and I'd love to hear what I'm missing.

subj: Why fast orbital trips need high thrust, in numbers
value: Build: Lambert + phasing study of delta-v vs trip time in GEO/LEO, plus burn time by thrust level
body:
Your point about 100x the thrust of in-space propulsion made me want to see the numbers, so I wrote a small study with a Lambert solver: how much delta-v it costs to reach a satellite on the same orbit, depending on how fast you need to get there.

In GEO, reaching a target 45 degrees ahead takes about 2.2 km/s in 7 hours but only 66 m/s if you can wait 4 days. An electric thruster would need over 4 months just to burn the 2.2 km/s, so fast trips aren't slower without high thrust, they're impossible. Code and tables: github.com/Venkat960407/transfer-tradeoff

subj: Catching rack hotspots before the 27 C alarm
value: Build: simulated data hall; peer-comparison + CUSUM catches airflow faults in ~70 min vs 8% for a 27 C threshold
body:
Aravolta detecting hotspots got me curious how much earlier you can catch one than a fixed temperature alarm, so I built a small simulated data hall: 40 racks, a minute of data each, with airflow faults, stuck sensors and a failing cooling unit injected.

Comparing each rack to the median of its row caught every airflow fault in about 70 minutes, while a 27 C threshold caught only 8% and gave about 11 false alarms a week. Comparing to the row is blind when the whole row warms, so that needed its own check. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/rack-hotspot-detect
